column2: Writing files through docker exec sh -c '...' broke on the first script holding single quotes: the outer quoting ended early ("(eval):94: unmatched '"); every file after that was sent base64-encoded through the same docker exec sh -c form

The release tarball cannot live in define/ (flat, no subdirectories), so it was unpacked to /home/user/se and the state directory and cwd put at /home/user/qtree, made before sideeye starts because a cwd must exist when it is resolved
preflight without an oracle refused boundary_without_oracle: quilt is a bash script that runs patch, mkdir, touch and others, so --oracle /usr/bin/strace is required for every run

The second preflight got 'File series fully applied' and recording_run_failed (exit 2 where 0 was expected): sideeye does not empty the state before the setup, the first run's .pc/ was still there, and setup.sh only wrote files; setup.sh now starts with find $S -mindepth 1 -delete

Leg D as first written (quilt pop -a, then quilt push -a, in a copy) would also go red under the controls for B and C: pop refuses a patch whose file was changed by hand, and push fails over a file already patched; changed before running to quilt pop -a -f and judging only the files of patches quilt lists as applied (from reading pop and push, not from a run)

quilt has no crash-recovery command; the one repair it names is quilt upgrade, which it asks for when .pc/ exists without .version (a kill between mkdir .pc and writing .version), so recover.sh runs that and nothing else
column3: cd tree; mkdir .pc; quilt applied -> 'Please run quilt upgrade'

column2: quilt writes while it reads: consistency_check touches .pc/applied-patches on quilt applied/series, so every quilt command in the checker except the recovery runs in a copy of the state

When the series is newer than .pc/applied-patches and they disagree, quilt series, applied and files all refuse ('The series file no longer matches the applied patches'), so legs B-D cannot learn the applied list through the tool; they fall back to reading .pc/applied-patches and leg A carries the refusal
/etc/quilt.quiltrc sets QUILT_PATCHES_PREFIX=yes, so quilt applied/series print patches/p1.diff while .pc/applied-patches holds p1.diff; the checker strips the prefix

explore refuses UNKNOWN child_touched_state_dir in the default mode: push runs its patch loop as a pipeline subshell, which runs patch(1) (writes a.txt and the backup), reaps it, then appends to .pc/applied-patches itself; strace shows the reap (wait4 = patch's pid) before the append, but sideeye counts the patch as still running
--observe supervised, which counts from outside, is a SETUP ERROR: no cgroup v2 it can create cgroups in (/sys/fs/cgroup is read-only, the user is not root, no sudo)
The refusal's next step (invoke the wrapped command as the operation instead) does not apply: quilt push -a is the operation, and the pipeline is inside quilt's own push script
Because the run was refused before any world, sideeye's checker gates (falsification, checker_rejects_initial_state) never ran; the checker's ability to fail rests on the hand-run controls only
column3: explore.json (checker: configured; this run stopped before the checker ran)

column2: Probes show the refusal is about the shape, not quilt: a subshell or an exec'd script whose child writes and is reaped before the parent writes is refused in both modes; bash -c with the subject writing itself is accepted under syscalls
A probe toml with an escaped quote in an argv string was refused (escape sequences are not part of the contract); the nested command went into a script file instead
In the default mode bash's own >> write is not in the shim's account (oracle_missed_operation); only --observe syscalls accepted the plain bash -c probe
